dashboard.description: What this app does, what its numbers mean, and what they do not.

div.h2: Riskability finds known vulnerabilities in the software your fleet actually has installed, using CVE databases you carry in by hand.
div.p: Built for search heads with no internet access. Nothing calls out: the vulnerability data is a file you build on a connected machine and import on Feed administration; inventory arrives from swinv through your forwarders.

An empty panel means nothing was found, not that there is nothing to find. A feed never imported, a host that stopped reporting, and a package no advisory covers all produce the same zero. Hence the three clocks below and the Coverage page.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_feedstate_lookup | search _key=current | eval days = round((now() - imported_at) / 86400, 1) | fields days

single.option: days since the CVE data was imported

search.query: | `riskability_hosts_seen` | stats max(host_last_scan) AS t | eval hours = round((now() - t) / 3600, 1) | fields hours

single.option: hours since any host last reported

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_matchstate_lookup | stats max(matched_at) AS t | eval hours = round((now() - t) / 3600, 1) | fields hours

single.option: hours since inventory was compared to the feed

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_hostcadence_lookup | eval is_late = if(tonumber(learned) = 1 AND tonumber(late) = 1, 1, 0) | eval is_on = if(tonumber(learned) = 1 AND tonumber(late) != 1, 1, 0) | eval is_new = if(isnull(learned) OR tonumber(learned) != 1, 1, 0) | stats sum(is_late) AS late, sum(is_on) AS on_schedule, sum(is_new) AS unlearned, count AS total | eval state = case(late > 0, "late", total = 0, "none", on_schedule = 0, "unlearned", 1=1, "calm") | eval verdict = case( total = 0, "No host has reported yet, so there is nothing to watch.", late > 0, "Some hosts have stopped contacting us for longer than their own observed pattern. Their findings are frozen at what they last reported and nothing is confirming them: a host that stopped reporting looks exactly like a host with nothing new. This is a collector, forwarder or machine fault, not a statement about the risk on those hosts.", on_schedule = 0, "Not enough of this fleet's rhythm has been observed to alarm yet. Every host here has contacted us fewer than three times, so there is nothing to compare its silence against. A fleet collected only after a deliberate change will sit here for a while, and that is the correct answer rather than a delayed alarm.", 1=1, "Every host with a learned rhythm is contacting us on its own schedule. That is a statement about collectors, not about risk: it means these numbers are as fresh as the hosts can make them, and nothing more. A host that last changed its software months ago and has confirmed it unchanged since is behaving normally and is not counted here.") | fields state, late, on_schedule, unlearned, total, verdict

| rest /servicesNS/nobody/riskability/saved/searches splunk_server=local | search eai:acl.app=riskability cron_schedule=* is_scheduled=1 | rex field=cron_schedule "^(?<sched_min>\d+)\s+(?<sched_hour>\S+)" | where sched_hour!="*" | eval label = replace(title, "^Riskability - ", "") | eval nxt = strptime(replace(next_scheduled_time, " UTC$", ""), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | eval away = nxt - now() | eval in_txt = case(isnull(away), "not scheduled", away < 3600, tostring(round(away/60)) . " min", away < 172800, tostring(round(away/3600)) . " h", 1=1, tostring(round(away/86400)) . " d") | eval one = label . ", next " . strftime(nxt, "%a %H:%M") . " (in " . in_txt . ")" | stats values(one) AS parts | eval line = mvjoin(parts, " · ") | fields line

panel.title: Hosts that have gone quiet against their own pattern

div.b: Judged against each host, never against one number for the fleet.
div.span: A machine scanned hourly is in trouble after two days; a machine scanned only when somebody changes it is fine after two months. This counts the collector going silent, never the software getting old. If a host here is collected on demand and you want it watched anyway, run swinv's heartbeat on a timer and keep the full collection on change: 309 bytes a scan removes the ambiguity entirely.

search.query: | rest /servicesNS/nobody/riskability/saved/searches splunk_server=local | search eai:acl.app=riskability cron_schedule=* is_scheduled=1 | rex field=cron_schedule "^(?<sched_min>\d+)\s+(?<sched_hour>\S+)" | where sched_hour=="*" | eval job_label = title | join type=left job_label [| rest /services/search/jobs splunk_server=local | search label="Riskability*" | eval job_label = label, pub = strptime(published, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%3N%z") | sort 0 - pub | stats first(isFailed) AS failed, first(runDuration) AS secs BY job_label] | eval label = replace(title, "^Riskability - ", "") | eval minute = tonumber(sched_min) | eval state = case(isnull(failed), "unknown", tonumber(failed) = 1, "failed", 1=1, "success") | eval seconds = round(tonumber(coalesce(secs, 0)), 2) | table label, minute, state, seconds | sort minute

viz.option: No scheduled searches were readable. This panel reads the app's own schedules through Splunk's REST endpoints, so an account that cannot see them gets nothing here rather than a picture of an idle pipeline.

html.div: Every number here is only as current as the oldest of those three. A fresh scan against a six-month-old feed finds six-month-old vulnerabilities.

div.b: A host with nothing new to report is not a host that stopped reporting.
div.span: swinv sends a heartbeat every scan - a digest of the component list - and the full list only when that digest changes, so most scans are a few hundred bytes rather than a few megabytes and only changed hosts are re-matched.

Last inventory above therefore tracks heartbeats, not full scans: it shows the host is still talking. Findings come from its last full component list, which may predate the last heartbeat and is still current, because the digest confirms nothing changed. Collectors that send no heartbeat still work; the app computes the digest itself.

div.b: Some hosts have been matched but their results have not been folded in.
div.span: Open counts for those hosts are stale-high and closing is withheld until the fold completes, so risk may be over-reported, never under-reported. Usually clears within the hour; if not, the pipeline has stopped and Admin shows which job.

search.query: index=`riskability_index_findings` sourcetype=riskability:findings record_type="match_receipt" earliest=0 latest=+10y _index_earliest=`riskability_stuck_window` _index_latest=now | stats max(match_run) AS match_run, sum(findings_produced) AS findings_produced BY hostname | where findings_produced > 0 | lookup riskability_matchstate_lookup hostname OUTPUT folded_run | eval acknowledged = if(isnotnull(folded_run) AND abs(tonumber(folded_run) - match_run) < 300, 1, 0) | where acknowledged == 0 | eval matched = strftime(match_run, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | eval folded = if(isnull(folded_run) OR folded_run="", "never", strftime(tonumber(folded_run), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")) | eval waiting = tostring(round(now() - match_run), "duration") | table hostname, matched, findings_produced, folded, waiting | rename hostname AS "Host", matched AS "Matched at", findings_produced AS "Findings the matcher reported", folded AS "Last folded in", waiting AS "Waiting"
| inputlookup riskability_openstate_host_lookup | stats sum(findings) AS n
| inputlookup riskability_openstate_host_lookup | stats sum(accepted) AS n

single.option: excluded on purpose, with a recorded reason

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_matchstate_lookup | stats sum(n_components) AS n

div.p: Not just the package manager: also container images, snap bases and chroots. It records the path of every copy, which separates a patched host from one with a stale copy in an image.

A PURL when a package manager installed it (pkg:deb/ubuntu/openssl), otherwise a CPE, which is most Windows software. PURLs come from package records; CPEs are inferred from a display name, so Windows findings are always low confidence.

div.b: Versions are compared using the right rules
div.p: Debian, RPM, Alpine, npm, Python, Maven and Go each order versions differently; text comparison gets it wrong. Where the comparison cannot be made properly the finding is marked low rather than asserted.

div.b: The finding is tracked over time
div.p: A finding that stops appearing is not automatically fixed. Newer version at the same path: mitigated. Gone: removed. Host stopped reporting: unknown. Silence is never success.

div.b: Reach decides the order of the work
div.p: The collector also records what is listening, which process holds the socket, and which containers run behind it. On this fleet that separates a few reachable findings from tens of thousands that are not; see Exposure. Reach re-orders the work, never shortens it: an unreachable vulnerability is still a vulnerability, and a host whose collector is too old to report ports is shown as not assessed, not safe.

panel.title: How MITRE ATT&CK fits, and where it loses information

div.div:
a specific vulnerability
in a specific product

the class of mistake
e.g. use-after-free

a pattern of attack
that abuses it

what an adversary
could then do

div.p: Every hop is a mapping MITRE publishes, and every hop loses information. A CVE with no CWE never reaches the matrix, so a technique missing from the ATT&CK page is not one you are safe from. One weakness maps to several techniques, so a vulnerability is drawn several times: the widths never add up to a total.

The chain says “this class of weakness enables that technique”. It does not say an adversary used it, or that it is exploitable in your environment. Use the KEV and EPSS columns on Findings for that: real-world exploitation rather than classification.

panel.title: How much survives the chain, right now

search.query: | `riskability_open_findings` | stats dc(cve_id) AS n | eval stage = "1. open CVEs" | append [| `riskability_finding_cwes` | stats dc(cve_id) AS n | eval stage = "2. have a CWE recorded"] | append [| `riskability_attack_surface` | stats dc(cve_id) AS n | eval stage = "3. reach a technique"] | eval series = stage | fields stage, series, n

viz.option: No open findings to trace through the chain.

html.div: The drop between these bars is what the mapping costs, not a defect. Read the ATT&CK page as “capabilities our open findings could hand an attacker”, never as a complete picture of exposure.

div.span: The numbers, and how stale they are.
The working list: what to patch, ranked by likelihood of exploitation rather than severity.
What was fixed, with the version change proving it, and what merely stopped being reported.
Lossy classification of what open findings could enable. Context, not evidence.
Which findings the network can reach, and which sit inside containers. Re-orders the work, never removes any of it.
One machine at a time, split by filesystem root.
What the app cannot see: ecosystems in the fleet the imported feed knows nothing about.
What a vulnerability actually is, offline. Every CVE id in every table on every page opens it here, so you never have to leave an air-gapped room to look one up.
Findings handled another way, and how. Excluded from every risk number and counted separately, so they are never hidden.
Import the offline CVE data, and download the builder that makes it.

dl.dd: The class of mistake. Most CVEs never get one assigned.
An attack pattern abusing such a weakness.
Adversary behaviour by tactic. Reached here through CWE and CAPEC, so lossily.
Identity read from package manager records. Precise.
Identity inferred where no package manager was involved. Weaker evidence.
Published estimate of exploitation within 30 days. Better for prioritising than severity.
CISA's exploited-in-the-wild list. The strongest signal available offline.
Filesystem the component was found in: host, snap base, container image, chroot.

Strength of the evidence, not severity. high: identity and version both from package records. informational: an upstream version range covering a distribution-maintained package, which the vendor may have patched by backport. low: identity inferred from a generated CPE, or the version could not be compared properly.
Who says the version is affected: distribution, upstream ecosystem, or NVD. Distributions win, because they backport.
One complete feed import. Findings match a single generation, never a half-written one.
